lesson.title: Automate the weekly report
lesson.subtitle: Extract, transform, load, on a schedule, safe to run again

video.title: Automate the weekly report
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: 12 registers; 3 hours; Counted twice. Mr Joseph beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Every Friday, our deputy head copies attendance from twelve registers into one report. It takes her three hours. And last month, she counted one class twice.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: automating the weekly report, with a pipeline that's safe to run again.

scenes.visual: A flow: Extract → Transform → Load → Report.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A data pipeline is a set of steps that runs on its own, again and again. Extract: read the data where it lives, like the registers. Transform: clean it and count it. Load: write the result where the report reads it.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Every evening at 6; Runs on its own; Ready each morning.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Then put it on a schedule: every evening at six, say. Nobody copies anything by hand, and the report is ready each morning.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: The connection drops; The database is busy; “?” instead of P or A.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But steps fail. The connection drops halfway. The database is busy. A register says question mark instead of P or A. A good pipeline expects this.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “Add the rows” (Rerun: counted twice) and “Replace the day's rows” (Rerun: same answer).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So every run must be safe to repeat. That's called idempotent: run it once or five times, and the answer is the same. The trick: replace the day's rows, don't just add more.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Passing fault: retry; Bad data: a person checks.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: And tell faults apart. A dropped connection passes: just retry. Bad data won't fix itself: set the row aside and ask a person.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: n = {} … Caption: Present pupils, counted for each class
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here's the transform step in Python. Read the register, and for every P, add one to that class's count. Five lines replace an hour of counting.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The load step failed halfway, and the pipeline runs again. Which way of loading is safe?

scenes.visual: One big value: 152, Pupils, after a rerun that adds: the school has 90.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Replace the day's rows: the rerun first clears Monday, then writes it again. Adding would count two classes twice, and the report would say a hundred and fifty-two pupils came, out of ninety.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Make a step fail; Retry; Replace: still 90.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, make a step fail and press Retry. With “Add the rows”, watch the report climb to a hundred and fifty-two. Switch to replace, and it stays at ninety however often it runs.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. One register says question mark for a pupil, and the transform step stops. Will pressing Retry fix it?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Extract, transform, load; On a schedule; Safe to run again; Retry, or ask a person. Takeaway bar: Run it twice; get the same answer.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: No: retrying fixes passing faults, not bad data. Remember: a pipeline extracts, transforms and loads, on a schedule. Make every run safe to repeat. And log every run, so you know what happened.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: One group reads; One counts; One writes the board; Rerun: counted twice?. Mr Joseph beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: run a “Human pipeline”. One group reads the registers aloud, one counts, and one writes the counts on the board. Then stop it halfway and run it again: did anyone count a class twice?

checkpoints.prompt: The load step failed halfway and the pipeline runs again. Which way of loading is safe?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — replacing the day's rows gives the same answer however many times it runs: it's idempotent.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — adding again writes the first classes twice. Replace the day's rows, so a rerun can't double-count.

checkpoints.prompt: A register says “?” instead of P or A, and the transform step stops. Will a retry fix it?

options.text: No: bad data needs a person to check it
Yes, if the network is faster

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the data itself is wrong, so every retry fails the same way. Set the row aside and ask the teacher.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — retries fix passing faults like a dropped connection. A “?” in the register stays a “?”: a person must check it.
